findings.evidence: Figure 6.2 axis annotation (rendered in-figure label): "SLO 2 s (TTFT budget)", with the shaded region labelled "SLO-violating region (> 2 s)" and the caption noting "the p95 TTFT ceiling (Table 4-2), not the 1.2 s design budget". Ch. 4 §4.3, PDF p. 106: "The two thresholds are not interchangeable: 1.2 s is the design budget, ≤ 2 s is the p95 ceiling the budget relaxes to, and any pass/fail judgement on a measured distribution is made against the p95 ceiling, not the budget."
findings.issue: The figure's own in-figure label calls the 2 s line the "TTFT budget", while the book's defined TTFT budget is 1.2 s (1.2 s = retrieval ~120 ms + prefill ~1.08 s) and 2 s is only the p95 ceiling. The caption of the very same figure contradicts the label, and Ch. 4 §4.3 explicitly forbids conflating the two. A reader who reads only the plotted annotation (the rendered label) will mis-attribute the SLO line.
findings.fix_instruction: Relabel the figure annotation from "SLO 2 s (TTFT budget)" to "p95 TTFT ceiling 2 s" (and keep the shaded band caption consistent), so that the in-figure text, the figure caption and Ch. 4 §4.3 use one term for each threshold.

findings.evidence: In-figure axis label (PDF p. 143, printed p. 119): "SLO 2 s (TTFT budget)". The caption on the same page states: "the 2 s request-latency line — the p95 TTFT ceiling (Table 4-2), not the 1.2 s design budget". Book convention, Ch. 4 (PDF p. 106, printed p. 82): "The two thresholds are not interchangeable: 1.2 s is the design budget, ≤ 2 s is the p95 ceiling the budget relaxes to".
findings.issue: The figure annotation attaches the word 'budget' to the 2 s line. Throughout the book 'TTFT budget' is reserved for the 1.2 s two-term design budget; 2 s is the p95 ceiling/SLO. The label therefore contradicts the figure's own caption and Ch. 4's explicitly load-bearing budget-vs-ceiling distinction — on the very figure that teaches percentile SLOs. A reader lifting the figure (its caption will not travel with it) reads 'TTFT budget = 2 s'.
findings.fix_instruction: Relabel the 2 s line to "SLO 2 s (p95 TTFT ceiling)" or drop the parenthetical so the figure matches its caption and Ch. 4's convention; optionally add a separate 1.2 s marker labelled 'design budget' to make the budget/ceiling pairing visible in the figure itself.

findings.page: 140 and 143 (PDF pages 140/553 and 143/553; printed pp. 116 and 119)
findings.chapter: Ch. 6 — Measuring What Matters (§6.1.1 and Fig. 6.2 caption)
findings.evidence: Instance 1, PDF p. 140 (printed 116): "the SLOs written against them are p95 TTFT ≤ 2 s and p95 TPOT ≤ 35 ms (Ch 4, Table 4-2)". Instance 2, PDF p. 143 (printed 119), Fig. 6.2 caption: "the p95 TTFT ceiling (Table 4-2), not the 1.2 s design budget". Table 4-2 itself (PDF pp. 98–101, printed 74–77) contains no p95 rows; its latency entries are "Prefill compute budget 1.08 s" and "Decode (TPOT) 25 ms/token". The p95 ceilings are actually stated in Table 4-1's Latency row (PDF p. 86, printed 62: "p95 TTFT ≤ 2 s, p95 TPOT ≤ 35 ms") and in the unnumbered Canonical Workload box (PDF p. 92, printed 68: "p95 ceiling ≤ 2 s"; "p95 ceiling ≤ 35 ms").
findings.issue: Both citations point at Table 4-2 for the p95 SLO ceilings, but the cited target does not contain those values (the 1.2 s / 25 ms budgets do sit in Table 4-2's neighbourhood; the p95 ceilings do not). The pointer resolves to the wrong element of the canonical reference set — it should target Table 4-1 and/or the Canonical Workload box. Recurrence sweep found exactly two instances, both in Ch. 6.
findings.fix_instruction: Change both citations to "(Ch 4, Table 4-1; Canonical Workload box)", or add explicit 'p95 TTFT ≤ 2 s' and 'p95 TPOT ≤ 35 ms' rows to Table 4-2 so the anchor provenance ledger actually carries the SLO ceilings every later chapter cites it for.

findings.chapter: Ch. 6 — Measuring What Matters: From Telemetry to Architecture Decisions
findings.evidence:
Workload metrics
rps · token profile · concurrency
... Label caveat: a concurrency entry in the workload box denotes the request rate λ that the traffic offers, not a concurrency value — request concurrency is derived on the serving side (in-flight = λ × W, Little’s law), the same classification this figure gives queue depth; see §6.1.1.
findings.issue: Figure/caption and prose conflict: the figure labels 'concurrency' as a workload metric, while the caption and §6.1.1 explicitly state that concurrency is not a workload input/value and that the entry denotes λ. This reuses one term with two meanings in a load-bearing diagnostic diagram.
findings.fix_instruction: Relabel the workload-box entry from 'concurrency' to 'arrival rate λ' or 'rps (λ; not concurrency)', then simplify the caption caveat so it no longer has to excuse a misleading label.
